business.title: Quanta Therapeutics Announces Presentation of QTX3034 Clinical Combination Data with Anti-EGFR and Chemotherapy in Colorectal Cancer (CRC) at ESMO and Fast Track Designation for Patients with KRAS G12
business.description: RADNOR, Pa. and SOUTH SAN FRANCISCO, Calif., Oct. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Quanta Therapeutics, a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company leading the development of innovative therapeutics for RAS-driven cancers, today announced that it will present clinical data for its oral, G12D-preferring multi-KRAS inhibitor QTX3034 in combination with cetuximab with or without FOLFOX chemotherapy in patients with CRC at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Annual Congress taking place October 23-27 in Madrid, Spain. Quanta also announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted Fast Track designation to QTX3034 for the treatment of KRASG12D-mutant CRC in combination with cetuximab, with or without FOLFOX chemotherapy, the same treatment regimens for which clinical data will be presented at ESMO.

business.title: Improving safety frameworks for generative AI and youth well-being policy
business.description: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) platforms have become increasingly prevalent in educational and social settings, impacting the social, emotional and mental well-being of youth users. AI platforms are often guided by ethical frameworks that promote user safety; however, these platforms do not always translate into youth-centered practices that account for the developmental, social and cultural needs of young people. Although current ethical frameworks have policies to prevent harm, there is considerable room for improvement in real-world practice. This policy brief examines how youth well-being policies were incorporated into the prompt-response practices in AI governance across five major platforms: OpenAI (ChatGPT), Google Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, Meta AI and Character.AI, focusing on areas such as prompt response, educational support, social context, culturally responsive design and age-appropriate interaction. Our observations highlight a gap between current policy frameworks and their practical application in the context of youth well-being. Addressing this disconnect requires the development of and strict adherence to standards that ensure generative AI platforms are responsive to the developmental, social and cultural needs of youth. The implementation of culturally responsive trauma-informed design recommendations could substantially improve AI design toward more ethical approaches, and also reduce potential harm to youth users. This Perspective evaluates youth well-being policies within AI governance, identifying gaps between ethical frameworks and practical applications. Recommendations emphasize culturally responsive design and trauma-informed approaches to enhance user safety and address developmental needs effectively.

science.title: Disentangling microbiota-dependent and -independent impacts of antibiotics on host physiology
science.description: Antibiotics are believed to affect host physiology by altering the gut microbiota. However, it remains unclear which effects of antibiotics are microbiota dependent and which are microbiota independent. Here we present a resource encompassing host and microbiota responses to antibiotic treatment and a computational tool with which to analyse them. Metagenomic and transcriptomic analyses of conventional and germ-free mice revealed that antibiotic administration routes and their combinations affect host and microbiota responses. We developed CompoRes—a computational tool that distinguishes the microbiota-independent impact of antibiotic-induced perturbations, revealing that antibiotics directly impact host physiology. We found that diurnal expression of major histocompatibility complex class II in the mouse colon is controlled by glucose via feeding. This pattern was lost during antibiotic treatment as vancomycin altered feeding behaviour in a microbiota-independent and evolutionarily conserved manner. Together, our study establishes a direct, non-microbial pathway by which antibiotics reshape host immunity and circadian physiology. Using a computational tool called CompoRes, the authors show that antibiotics can alter feeding behaviour, immunity and circadian regulation, revealing a non-microbial pathway by which antibiotic treatment reshapes host physiology.

science.title: Stepwise and chemoselective installation of carbon substituents at silicon atoms via monobromination of hydrosilanes
science.description: Although organosilicon compounds containing different carbon substituents are ubiquitous in synthetic chemistry, their preparation is challenging. Laboratory synthesis commonly relies on the sequential substitution of tetrachlorosilane or tetraalkoxysilanes, producing complex mixtures that require demanding purification. This arises from limited control over nucleophilic substitution in functionalized silanes containing three or four (identical) leaving groups. Here we introduce an experimentally straightforward and reliable procedure for the preparation of both hetero- and homoleptic silanes using an overlooked monobromination of primary and secondary hydrosilanes. An equimolar amount of elemental bromine converts a Si–H bond into an Si–Br bond without ‘overbromination’. This step also shows exceptional functional-group tolerance to existing substituents at the silicon atom. Unsaturated moieties as well as heteroatom and heteroaryl groups are compatible. When performed in an iterative fashion, multihydrosilanes can be selectively converted into secondary, tertiary and quaternary silanes with two, three or four different carbon substituents in high yields. These functionalized silicon building blocks are relevant to synthetic chemistry as well as applied chemistry materials. Heteroleptic organosilanes with four different substituents are prepared by a selective and simple method based on the controlled monobromination of multihydrosilanes. This approach avoids the limitations of conventional methods, tolerates diverse functional groups and enables iterative access to highly substituted silanes in excellent yields.
